subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw define and own a runtime-neutral agent-core protocol for no-Node embedded ports, or should MimiClaw-style ports stay external until a narrower core API gap is proven?
rationale: Current code has only Node-hosted runtime and in-process plugin/harness seams, so the remaining step is a product/API ownership decision rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Keep canonical design issue
options.body: Use this issue to decide the protocol boundary, schemas, conformance tests, and external-port expectations before accepting implementation PRs.

options.title: Defer to external ports
options.body: Close or narrow this only if maintainers decide no-Node runtimes should remain independent projects unless they need a specific plugin/API seam.

options.title: Split a smaller RFC
options.body: Open a narrower maintainer-owned RFC for the first shared schema or conformance boundary and keep this issue as background context.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical design issue
recommendation.body: Use this issue to decide the protocol boundary, schemas, conformance tests, and external-port expectations before accepting implementation PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The inspected history and existing issue comments place Peter closest to the runtime/platform boundary and harness direction.
